title: Concrete Slab Calculator
metaTitle: Concrete Slab Calculator: Bags and Yards of Concrete
metaDescription: Calculate cubic yards and bags of concrete needed for slabs, patios, and footings. Includes 60-lb and 80-lb bag options and waste allowance.

inputs.label: Depth / Thickness
inputs.help: Most patios and sidewalks are 4 inches thick.

constants.label: Bag yield (cubic feet per bag)
constants.note: Typical yield: 80-lb bag = 0.60 ft³, 60-lb bag = 0.45 ft³. Check the bag label.

testCases.name: 6 × 6 ft at 6 in, waste 0, yield 0.45 (60-lb bags)

content.intro: Pouring concrete leaves no room for running out halfway through, because a cold joint weakens the finished slab. This calculator helps you determine whether you should mix pre-packaged bags in a wheelbarrow or order ready-mix concrete delivered by the truckload. Enter the length, width, and thickness of your slab, and the tool will calculate the exact cubic yards and total bags required. A ten percent waste buffer covers uneven sub-grade excavation and spillage along the forms. Measure your framed area carefully before ordering. Results are estimates — confirm with your supplier before you buy.
content.howItWorks: The calculator multiplies length × width × thickness (thickness converted from inches to feet) to find cubic feet, then divides by 27 for cubic yards. Bags needed = ceil(cubic feet × (1 + waste%) / bag yield). Formula: cubic feet = L × W × (D ÷ 12). Cubic yards = cubic feet ÷ 27. Bags = ⌈cubic feet × (1 + waste%) ÷ yield⌉.

examples.title: A 10 by 10 foot patio slab at 4 inches thick
examples.text: Length 10 ft, width 10 ft, thickness 4 in. Cubic feet = 10 × 10 × (4 ÷ 12) = 33.33 ft³. Cubic yards = 33.33 ÷ 27 = 1.23 yd³. Using 80-lb bags (0.60 ft³ yield) with 10% waste: bags = ⌈33.33 × 1.1 ÷ 0.60⌉ = ⌈61.1⌉ = 62 bags.

commonMistakes: Entering slab thickness in feet instead of inches — 4 inches is 0.33 feet, not 4.
Forgetting to excavate deep enough for a gravel drainage base under the concrete.
Underestimating how heavy bagged concrete is — 60 bags of 80-lb mix weighs over two tons.
Not adding waste allowance for ground that dips below the bottom of the form boards.

faq.q: How thick should a concrete slab be?
faq.a: A 4-inch slab is standard for walkways, residential patios, and shed bases. Heavy vehicle driveways usually require 5 to 6 inches with rebar.

faq.q: When is it better to order ready-mix concrete instead of bags?
faq.a: If your project requires more than 1 to 1.5 cubic yards (about 45 to 70 eighty-pound bags), ordering ready-mix delivery saves significant manual labor.

faq.q: How many 80-pound bags of concrete are in a cubic yard?
faq.a: It takes 45 eighty-pound bags (yield 0.60 ft³ each) to equal one cubic yard (27 ft³). Always add 5 to 10 percent for waste.

faq.q: How many 60-pound bags of concrete are in a cubic yard?
faq.a: It takes 60 sixty-pound bags (yield 0.45 ft³ each) to make one cubic yard.
